doc.title: Harold Mabern interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 31, 2010

title: Jazz musicians' wide range of interests and Oscar Peterson on Herbie
summary: He says musicians excel outside music, tells of Oscar Peterson's video and Herbie Hancock, and lists doctors and attorneys among players.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Well just to wrap up, I can tell that you’re proud to be a jazz musician, and you’re proud of your fellow jazz musicians.
I mean you were saying yesterday that jazz musicians are some of the most intelligent, well rounded people.

Right. They really are. Because like I said any subject matter you name, any one, anything, they’re doing it somewhere. Ophthalmology, they’re doing it. Optometry? Speak a different language? They’re doing it. Herbie Hancock, electrical engineer,

because I remember once he was talking because Oscar Peterson had a tremendous respect for Herbie. He said it in print. And he was talking about it one time. I got this video called “In the Key of Oscar.” This is a very good video. I don’t know if you can get it in the States, you might have to call the Institute of Canada in Toronto and get it. Mulgrew has it, and it’s Oscar doing a reunion with his family members because he had been estranged from a couple of his kids because he was so busy traveling and they couldn’t understand I can’t be here with you because I’m trying to go out here to make this money so I can send you to the kind of —. You know what I mean. But they had to come and get him. And Oscar was talking about a lot of stuff and like he said, “No, I don’t want to intimidate nobody, he said, but if you get in my way I’m going to run over you musically.” And he cleared that up. You know what I’m saying. But he was talking about Herbie Hancock. Herbie said, “Well you know about the electric piano.” And Herbie said, “Well you know, Oscar, I think Oscar is scared of the electric piano.” Oscar: “you tell Herbie Hancock he better hope and pray that I don’t come out.” Because Oscar knew a lot about the electric piano because in his studio he had every electrical instrument he could. But, “I don’t want to do an electric piano date for the sake of doing it.” He said, “I can do three trio dates in one day in less than three hours.” But he said, “No Herbie’s been baiting me on to do it, but he has tremendous respect for Herbie. You know what I mean. But I feel good that I’ve had a chance to be around some great people. I wish I could have been around Art Tatum. I never saw Art Tatum in person. I never saw my other hero Nat Cole in person. I did see Bird but not up close and personal. I did see him standing outside the club. So I feel I’ve been blessed because as I said before, musicians are, man, wide range. Jimmy Heath, computer; Frank Foster, computer; Ben Brown, computer; Dr. Denny Zeitlin, practicing psychiatrist; Dr. Art Davis, psychiatrist; Peter LaRoca, attorney at law. The list just goes on and on. Sir Charles Thompson could be a golf pro; Joe Williams, golf; Lou Donaldson, Jimmy Cobb, Keter Betts, Freddie Green, Ray Brown, mean with the stick. Ray Brown, heck of a businessman. You know, Hubert Laws, go out and do concerts with Jean Pierre Rampal played that stuff, and they couldn’t play here. Hubert Laws, you know, that flute. You know Jesus, Julius Baker I think was principal flautist with the Philharmonic. So jazz musicians, Herbie just did a George Gershwin classical Chopin type concert with a Chinese piano player named Lang Lang. And Herbie took off five months and got a teacher just to mainly deal with certain fingerings. But he practiced diligent and Garnett Brown, another one of my home towners, great trombone player, unsung hero, his name is Garnett Brown. He did some orchestrations for Herbie. He did the soundtrack for a movie called “Harlem Nights” with Richard Pryor. He wrote the music for that.
